text: Harness: executor backends - built-in tool loop, or delegate coding leaves to Claude Code / Codex in a worktree
description: Executor interface: execute(idea, compiledContext, worktree, budget) -> {diff, commands run, claimed evidence, usage}. Backend 1: the existing AI SDK tool loop (read/search/str_replace/run_command). Backend 2: headless CLI agents (claude -p / codex exec --json) in a disposable git worktree; reuse the Codex adapter with authoritative telemetry from 02e512d5. The harness, not the CLI agent, writes results to the graph. Lets strong coding agents do the code while the harness keeps the loop, context and verification.

status.comment: harness.json executor.backend = builtin (AI SDK tool loop on the executor role model, default) | claude-code | codex; packages/loop-worker/src/cli-executors.ts. Claude Code: `claude -p` with --json-schema (execution schema), --strict-mcp-config, --setting-sources user, acceptEdits + allowlist, --max-budget-usd; its reported cost joins the cycle cost. Codex: `codex exec --json --ephemeral --sandbox workspace-write --ignore-user-config --output-schema <execution schema> --output-last-message`, usage summed from turn.completed events, priced from harness.json prices. Both run in the loop's execution path (loop.worktreePath when set) with AIMPARENCY_ALLOW_STOP=1, get no MCP servers (the harness alone writes the graph), share one process runner (own timeout; spawn errors settle instead of hanging), and are checked by the harness verifier like the built-in executor. Evidence: cli-executors.test (args, env, cwd, usage/cost, error/invalid/missing binary, codex exit code), cycle.test with the claude-code backend end to end, loop-worker 35/35; real-CLI probes in a scratch dir both returned valid structured results (Claude Code with Haiku $0.005, Codex default model ~15k tokens). Not done by design: creating disposable worktrees per cycle — a fresh worktree lacks installed dependencies, so tests could not run; isolation stays the loop's worktreePath option.
